## Dieses Dokument

- Titel: Brief von Stefan Zweig an Hannah; Altmann, Manfred Altmann [September 1941], SZ-AAL/B1.164
- Signatur: SZ-AAL/B1.164
- Datum: 09.1941
- Objekttyp: Brief
- Umfang: 3 Scans

pages.transcription:
Dear Hannah & Manfred, we have your letter of August 20th today Sept 4th I am sorry
that the house in Bath gives you so much trouble - especially as
I doubt more and more that we shall ever see it again. Please do
not spare yourself and do not too much work, the coming times
will ask from us all our strength. As to Lotte's box I wrote
you already that you shall not worry too much; I am convinced
that I shall have with him serious discussions and I do not wish that you
shall be mixed in my personal troubles. Thanks so much to have given the
manuscript of my Balzac to Lotte; it would be wonderful if I could
get it one day and continue my work! You are really too kind! You cannot
imagine how I am longing to work quietly. Lotte will write you about our
intention to go to Petropolis; I want absolutely a few months rest and
in any case I shall not give any lectures before spring. We cannot see
any more trunks, suitcases, we are tired of hotels, of changes. -
I wish I could report to you that Lotte is quite right. Unfortunately she
has seldom a quiet night and I hope only that the treatment will finally
give her complete recovery. It is perhaps also the nomadic life with its
changes of climate and surroundings which was not favorable to us both
I have finished the autobiography in the greatest strain only to
finish it before leaving New York and will now work on it quietly. At
least six month we hope to stay in Petropolis - you know how I like
to travel but now we feel we have overdone it. It will be an absolute
relieved life without society, theatres and (the only thing I miss) without
books and we even do not start to think what we shall do afterwards.
Here in Rio the first news we received was that the poor Count Hoya
died on the consequence of an angina (streptococcic poisoning) -
Fritzi's have flowers but we have not yet seen him. He has made a
book on the president and will get much money out of the funds:
you know how I admire his ability. I have seen so many of the best
in New York unable to earn a cent that I find it masterly how he
always invents new possibilities to live largely. Give Edelmann my
kindest regards. My indifference against books etc. comes from the
conviction that I shall never see them and I wish you would keep
them as the best of them for you. We are all very confident in
the final victory, more, much more than ever before but there is no
[Randnotiz links:] doubt that it will take some time - some years perhaps - as the enormous preparation of
the United States will be in full swing but from now on there every day is for Britain
and you in England will have still much burdens to bear. I wish you well.
pages.notes: Handschriftlicher Brief auf Hotelpapier (Hotel Central, Rio de Janeiro). Die Randnotiz links ist vertikal geschrieben. Die Tinte ist blau.

result.confidence_notes: Der Text ist sehr gut lesbar, trotz der handschriftlichen Kursivschrift. Die Randnotiz wurde korrekt zugeordnet.
